meta.title: Landscaping in Royal Oak, MI | HD Landscape
meta.description: Landscaping for Royal Oak, MI homes: design, tree trimming, cleanups and upkeep around old trees, small lots and tricky soil. Free itemized estimates.

hero.title: Big trees, small lots, **sand here, clay there.**
hero.lede: Royal Oak calls itself the City of Trees, and your yard probably agrees: old shade, a house from before 1960, and ground that may be sand or heavy clay depending on the side of town. HD Landscape plans around all of that, then plants the yard and looks after it.
chips: We know which trees are the city’s

about.title: Six in ten homes here were built before 1960.
body: Census figures put the median home at 1956, and the 1950s left more houses standing than any other decade. Shrubs planted along those foundations have had decades to outgrow the windows, and the shade trees have had just as long to spread over the beds. A lot of good work here begins with deciding what comes out.

Styles mix, even inside one neighborhood. Vinsetta Park has Tudor, Colonial and Arts and Crafts homes on curving streets, and a bed that suits one can look wrong on the next. In the one family zone the minimum lot is 6,000 square feet and a house can sit 25 feet back, so the front yard is seen up close from the sidewalk. A sloppy bed line has nowhere to hide.

Then there is the water. The Red Run, the stream the city grew up around, now runs in pipe under town, and many street drain covers are built to hold rain back in a storm so the sewers do not back up. Where your roof and lawn send water matters here.

points.title: A soil line between Woodward and Main
points.body: Downtown and much of the east side sit on sandy Thetford soil, while the west side around Woodward is heavier Blount and Lenawee. Sand drains fast and dries out. Heavy ground stays wet. The plant list and the watering plan depend on which one you have.

points.title: Trees that are not yours
points.body: A tree in the lawn strip along the curb is a city street tree, and work on it goes through the city. Planting here goes back to the 1930s, so those trees often set the light for the whole front yard. We plan around them.

points.title: Close quarters
points.body: Zoning lets a house sit about five feet from the side line, so the side yard can be little more than a walk. Materials come through in small loads, and where the trailer sits is best settled before the crew arrives.

points.title: Leaves and the street
points.body: Restricted drain covers on residential streets have only two or four slots, and leaves clog them quickly. Fall work also has to fit the city’s leaf trucks, so the gutter has to stay clear and a cleanup has to land around your street’s pickup.

logistics.title: A Royal Oak job starts with what is yours and what is the city’s.
body: On the walk, Jake sorts out what is yours and what is the city’s, looks at the soil and the water, and tells you what he would do and what he would leave alone. The estimate comes itemized, so you can go over it line by line with no pressure to say yes.

On the day, the crew shows up when we said. During leaf season the city asks for cars off the street so its trucks can reach the curb, which means parking and deliveries have to work around your block’s pickup day. We leave the walks and the drive clean.

faq.q: Does HD Landscape do landscaping in Royal Oak?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape is a landscaper based in St. Clair Shores that works in Royal Oak on homes and commercial properties. That includes [landscape design](/landscape-design-royal-oak-mi/), [tree trimming](/tree-trimming-royal-oak-mi/), [yard cleanups](/yard-cleanup-royal-oak-mi/), [pressure washing](/pressure-washing-royal-oak-mi/), [sod](/sod-installation/), [hedge trimming](/hedge-trimming/) and [monthly maintenance](/monthly-landscape-maintenance/). Call or text Jake at [(586) 718-8762](tel:+15867188762) for a free estimate.

faq.q: Is the soil in Royal Oak clay or sand?
faq.a: Both, depending on where you live. USDA soil maps show sandy Thetford ground through downtown and much of the east side, and heavier Blount and Lenawee ground on the west side around Woodward. The ground around an older house has often been moved or filled, so the map is only a start. The spot itself decides the plant list.

faq.q: Why does my street pond after a heavy rain?
faq.a: It is built to. Many Royal Oak streets have restricted drain covers with only two or four slots, which slow rain into the sewers so they do not back up into basements. The ponding is temporary and usually under 12 inches at the road edge, but a yard that drains to the street may have to hold its water for a while. Keep leaves and clippings off those covers, and if water sits against the house, [yard grading](/yard-grading/) is the place to start.

faq.q: Can I get a free street tree in Royal Oak?
faq.a: You can request one. If a tree was removed from the right of way, or there is an open space beside your property, the city takes requests for a free street tree in the strip along the curb. The city’s arborist picks the species, and programs change, so ask the city what is open now. Either way, lay out the beds behind it for the size it will reach, not the size it came.

faq.q: What landscaping work do you not do?
faq.a: Sprinklers and lawn aeration are not on our list. In Royal Oak, neither are city street trees, because that work goes through the city. Smaller trees on private land we can handle, and Jake hands the big removals to a tree company.

faq.q: Can you look after the yard once the project is done?
faq.a: Yes. [Monthly landscape maintenance](/monthly-landscape-maintenance/) can cover beds, weeding, shaping shrubs and edging, and what a visit covers is set on your estimate. A [spring or fall cleanup](/yard-cleanup-royal-oak-mi/) handles the heavy work, timed around the city’s leaf trucks and its curbside yard waste dates.
